Scenario: Valid login with standard_user
Preconditions: Browser is open on the SauceDemo login page
Steps: Open https://www.saucedemo.com | Enter standard_user in the Username field | Enter the shared password in the Password field | Click Login
Test_Data: standard_user / secret_sauce (shared password published on the SauceDemo login page)
Expected_Result: Login succeeds: user is redirected to the inventory page (URL contains inventory.html) and the product list, cart icon and menu button are visible

Scenario: Invalid password for a valid username is rejected
Preconditions: Browser is open on the SauceDemo login page
Steps: Enter standard_user in the Username field | Enter an incorrect password in the Password field | Click Login | Observe the error banner and URL
Expected_Result: Login is rejected: user stays on the login page (URL unchanged), no inventory access, and the error banner reads Epic sadface: Username and password do not match any user in this service

Scenario: Empty required fields show the correct validation messages
Preconditions: Browser is open on the SauceDemo login page with both fields empty
Steps: Leave Username and Password empty and click Login | Observe the error message | Enter standard_user in Username, leave Password empty and click Login | Observe the error message
Test_Data: Empty string in Username; then empty string in Password
Expected_Result: First attempt is blocked with the error banner Epic sadface: Username is required; second attempt is blocked with the error banner Epic sadface: Password is required; in both cases the user stays on the login page and no navigation occurs

Scenario: locked_out_user cannot log in
Preconditions: Browser is open on the SauceDemo login page
Steps: Enter locked_out_user in the Username field | Enter the shared password in the Password field | Click Login
Expected_Result: Login is rejected: user stays on the login page and the error banner reads Epic sadface: Sorry, this user has been locked out.; the inventory page is never reachable

Scenario: SQL-injection-style string is rejected safely
Preconditions: Browser is open on the SauceDemo login page
Steps: Enter a SQL-injection-style string in the Username field | Enter the same string in the Password field | Click Login | Observe the response
Expected_Result: Login is rejected with the standard invalid-credentials error; no database error message, stack trace, blank page or redirect to the inventory page occurs; user stays on the login page

Scenario: Whitespace padding and case sensitivity of credentials
Preconditions: Browser is open on the SauceDemo login page
Steps: Enter a leading-space variant like ' standard_user' with the correct password and click Login | Enter STANDARD_USER with the correct password and click Login | Enter standard_user with SECRET_SAUCE (wrong case) and click Login
Test_Data: Whitespace-padded username; ALL-CAPS username; wrong-case password variants of valid credentials
Expected_Result: None of the variants log in: credentials must match the published values exactly (case-sensitive, no whitespace trimming); the standard invalid-credentials error appears each time and the user stays on the login page

Scenario: Error message wording, styling and dismiss behaviour
Preconditions: Browser is open on the SauceDemo login page
Steps: Trigger an invalid-login attempt with a wrong password and read the banner text | Trigger the empty-username error and read the banner text | Click the X button on the banner
Expected_Result: Error banners use the exact published wording (Epic sadface: Username and password do not match any user in this service / Epic sadface: Username is required), are shown in a red banner with a warning icon, and clicking X dismisses the banner and clears the invalid field state

Scenario: Password field masks the typed password
Preconditions: Browser is open on the SauceDemo login page
Steps: Type the shared password into the Password field character by character | Observe the field while typing | Check the field value visually after typing
Test_Data: secret_sauce typed into the Password field
Expected_Result: Password characters are masked as dots or asterisks while typing; the password is never displayed in plain text in the field or anywhere on screen

Scenario: Item count on the inventory page
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user and viewing the inventory page
Steps: Open the inventory page | Count the product cards listed from top to bottom
Expected_Result: Exactly 6 product cards are displayed, each showing an image, product name, description, price and an Add to cart control

Scenario: All product images load correctly
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user and viewing the inventory page
Steps: Open the inventory page | Inspect each of the 6 product image slots one by one
Expected_Result: All 6 product images load and are fully visible; no broken-image icons, empty slots or alt-text-only placeholders appear

Scenario: Product name and price are consistent between list and detail page
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user and viewing the inventory page
Steps: Note the name, price and description of one product in the list | Click that product name to open its detail page | Compare the values | Go back and repeat for a second product
Expected_Result: For every product checked, the name, price and description on the detail page exactly match the list view, and all prices use the format $X.XX

Scenario: Add and remove an item from the inventory list updates the cart badge
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user; cart is empty (no badge shown)
Steps: Click Add to cart on one product | Observe the button text and the cart badge | Click Remove on the same product | Observe the button text and the cart badge again
Expected_Result: After adding, the button changes to Remove and the cart badge shows 1; after removing, the button returns to Add to cart and the cart badge disappears

Scenario: Sort products by Name (A to Z)
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user and viewing the inventory page in default order
Steps: Open the Sort dropdown | Select Name (A to Z) | Read the product names from top to bottom
Expected_Result: Products are reordered so product names are in ascending alphabetical order from top to bottom

Scenario: Sort products by Name (Z to A)
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user and viewing the inventory page
Steps: Open the Sort dropdown | Select Name (Z to A) | Read the product names from top to bottom
Expected_Result: Products are reordered so product names are in descending alphabetical order from top to bottom, exactly the reverse of the A to Z order

Scenario: Sort products by Price (low to high)
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user and viewing the inventory page
Steps: Open the Sort dropdown | Select Price (low to high) | Read the prices from top to bottom
Expected_Result: Product prices appear in ascending numeric order (cheapest first); products with equal prices keep a stable relative order

Scenario: Sort products by Price (high to low)
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user and viewing the inventory page
Steps: Open the Sort dropdown | Select Price (high to low) | Read the prices from top to bottom
Expected_Result: Product prices appear in descending numeric order (most expensive first), exactly the reverse of the low to high order

Scenario: Open a product detail page and return with the back button
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user and viewing the inventory page
Steps: Click a product name (not the image) | Verify the detail page content | Click the Back to products button
Expected_Result: Clicking the name opens that product's detail page with matching name, image, description and price; Back to products returns to the inventory list with the previous cart state (badge count) preserved

Scenario: Add to cart from the product detail page
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user; cart is empty
Steps: Open any product detail page | Click Add to cart | Observe the button text and the cart badge | Open the cart and verify the item is listed
Expected_Result: The button changes to Remove and the cart badge increments to 1; the cart lists that product with the correct name and price

Scenario: Add multiple items and verify badge count and cart contents
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user; cart is empty
Steps: Add three different products from the inventory list | Check the cart badge after each addition | Open the cart | Verify the listed items
Test_Data: standard_user; three different products of choice
Expected_Result: The badge increments 1, 2, 3 as items are added; the cart lists exactly the three selected items with correct names and prices and no duplicates

Scenario: Remove an item from the cart
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user; cart contains 3 items
Steps: Open the cart | Click Remove on one item | Observe the remaining cart list | Return to the inventory page and check the badge
Expected_Result: The selected item is removed immediately, the other two items remain with correct details, and the cart badge decreases from 3 to 2

Scenario: Continue shopping returns to the inventory with the cart intact
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user; cart contains at least 1 item
Steps: Open the cart | Click Continue shopping | Check the inventory page and the cart badge
Test_Data: standard_user; at least 1 item in cart
Expected_Result: User is returned to the inventory page, the cart badge shows the same count as before, and previously added items remain in the cart

Scenario: Cart contents persist after a page refresh
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user; cart contains 2 items
Steps: Open the cart and confirm the 2 items | Refresh the page with the browser reload action | Check the cart contents and badge after the refresh
Expected_Result: After the refresh the cart still lists the same 2 items with correct names and prices, and the badge still shows 2; no items are lost or duplicated

Scenario: Valid checkout information shows a correct order overview
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user; at least 1 item in cart
Steps: Add items to the cart and open the cart | Click Checkout | Enter First name, Last name and Postal code | Click Continue | Review the checkout overview page
Test_Data: standard_user; First name: Test; Last name: User; Postal code: 12345
Expected_Result: The form is accepted and the checkout overview shows exactly the cart items with correct names and prices; the Item total equals the sum of item prices; Tax and Total lines are displayed; Back, Cancel and Finish actions are available

Scenario: Each required checkout field left empty is rejected
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user; at least 1 item in cart; checkout information form is open
Steps: Leave all three fields empty and click Continue | Observe the error | Fill First name only, leave Last name empty and click Continue | Observe the error | Fill First and Last name, leave Postal code empty and click Continue | Observe the error
Test_Data: Empty values for First name, Last name and Postal code (one run per field)
Expected_Result: Each attempt stays on the form with the specific message: Error: First Name is required, then Error: Last Name is required, then Error: Postal Code is required; the overview page is never reached until all three fields are filled

Scenario: Special characters in checkout name fields
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user; at least 1 item in cart; checkout information form is open
Steps: Enter special characters in First name | Enter special characters in Last name | Enter 12345 in Postal code | Click Continue | Check how the values are displayed on the overview
Test_Data: First name: O'Brien-Smith! @#; Last name: Doe & Co. <tag>; Postal code: 12345
Expected_Result: The form accepts the input without a crash or raw error page; the user reaches the overview; the entered values are displayed exactly as typed with no silent stripping of characters and no HTML/script rendering

Scenario: Order overview total and tax calculation
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user; cart contains items whose prices were recorded from the inventory page
Steps: Add items with known prices to the cart | Reach the checkout overview | Compare Item total with the sum of the listed item prices | Check the Tax line and the Total line
Test_Data: standard_user; two or more items with prices recorded from the inventory list
Expected_Result: Item total equals the exact sum of the cart item prices to the cent; Tax is derived from the item total; Total equals Item total + Tax; all amounts use $ formatting with two decimal places

Scenario: Cancel checkout returns to the cart with items intact
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user; cart contains items; checkout overview is open
Steps: Reach the checkout overview | Click Cancel | Check the cart page
Expected_Result: User is returned to the cart page, all cart items are still present with correct quantities and prices, and no order is created

Scenario: Finish places the order and shows the confirmation page
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user; cart contains items; checkout overview is open with valid information
Steps: On the checkout overview click Finish | Observe the confirmation page | Navigate back to products and check the cart state
Test_Data: standard_user; valid checkout data from TC-023
Expected_Result: An order confirmation page is displayed with the message Thank you for your order! and a back-to-products action; the cart is emptied (no badge); no payment information is requested at any point

Scenario: Logout ends the session
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user and viewing the inventory page
Steps: Click the hamburger menu button | Click Logout | Observe the resulting page and URL
Expected_Result: User is redirected to the login page; the inventory and cart are no longer visible, and accessing them again requires a new login

Scenario: Browser back button after logout cannot reopen the inventory
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user, then logged out (currently on the login page)
Steps: After logging out press the browser Back button | Observe the resulting page | If redirected, attempt to open the inventory URL directly
Expected_Result: The protected inventory page is not displayed with the previous session; the user remains on (or is redirected back to) the login page and no authenticated content is visible

Scenario: About and Reset App State menu links
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user; cart contains at least 1 item and some item buttons show Remove
Steps: Open the hamburger menu | Click About | Return to the application | Open the menu again | Click Reset App State | Check the cart badge and the item buttons on the inventory page
Test_Data: standard_user; item(s) added to the cart before the reset
Expected_Result: About opens the Sauce Labs website without breaking the app; Reset App State returns the app to its initial state: cart badge gone, all product buttons back to Add to cart, cart empty

Scenario: problem_user compared against standard_user (exploratory)
Preconditions: Logged out; the same flows were already executed once as standard_user for comparison
Steps: Log in as problem_user | Browse the inventory list (names, images, prices, button states) | Add an item and open the cart | Compare every observation with the identical steps performed as standard_user
Test_Data: problem_user / secret_sauce; same flows previously executed with standard_user
Expected_Result: Behaves like standard_user: same layout, same 6 products with correct names, prices and images, and the same add-to-cart and cart behaviour; any deviation from the standard_user behaviour is logged as a defect

Scenario: visual_user compared against standard_user (exploratory)
Preconditions: Logged out; the same pages were already viewed once as standard_user for comparison
Steps: Log in as visual_user | Browse inventory, a product detail page and the cart | Compare layout, alignment, colours, fonts and images with the same pages seen as standard_user
Test_Data: visual_user / secret_sauce; same pages viewed with standard_user
Expected_Result: Behaves like standard_user: identical layout, alignment, colours, images and content on the same pages; any visual deviation from the standard_user rendering is logged as a defect

Scenario: Basic responsive layout and UI consistency check
Preconditions: Logged in as standard_user and viewing the inventory page
Steps: Resize the browser window to a narrow width around 375 px | Check that content is readable and all controls are reachable | Resize back to a desktop width around 1366 px | Re-check the layout
Test_Data: standard_user; viewport widths of approximately 375 px and 1366 px
Expected_Result: At both widths the page stays usable: product names, prices, the Add to cart buttons, menu and cart badge do not overlap or get clipped, and at desktop width the page requires no horizontal scrolling
